name: Panhandle & Santa Fe Railway
description: Panhandle & Santa Fe Railway was a principal Santa Fe operating subsidiary in Texas, serving the Texas Panhandle, West Texas and adjoining territory. It remained a separate corporate operating company through the diesel era until its merger into ATSF on August 1, 1965.

statistics.intro: Two snapshots compare P&SF in the first series-production diesel era with its final full year before absorption into Santa Fe.
notes: Route-mile figures use the nearest verified Santa Fe/P&SF mileage references available for the corresponding periods.
Values marked ≈ are working estimates supplied for this project, derived from contemporary operating scale and comparable Santa Fe-system data; they are not direct carrier-specific counts.

P&SF was a large operating railroad, but much of its equipment was supplied or owned by the Santa Fe system. Low or zero P&SF-owned-equipment figures do not describe the equipment actually operated on P&SF lines. The locomotive and non-locomotive rolling-stock values here remain the supplied estimates.

history: Panhandle & Santa Fe was one of the two major Santa Fe operating subsidiaries in Texas. It was chartered in 1886 as the Southern Kansas Railway Company of Texas and renamed Panhandle & Santa Fe Railway in 1914. It operated a large network across the Texas Panhandle, West Texas and adjoining territory. Much of that network initially ran through leased subsidiaries. In 1948, most affiliated Texas properties were consolidated into P&SF, with the Kansas City, Mexico & Orient Railway Company of Texas and Rio Grande, El Paso & Santa Fe remaining exceptions.

P&SF remained a separate corporate operating company through the diesel era, using equipment supplied by the Santa Fe system. It merged into the Atchison, Topeka & Santa Fe Railway on August 1, 1965, placing its network directly in the Santa Fe branch of today's BNSF genealogy.
paintSchemesIntro: Diesel locomotives operating on P&SF lines were supplied by the Santa Fe system and carried Santa Fe paint schemes. See the Santa Fe page for the shared system paint history.
